messages:
maria: Kickoff prep for HealthCo POC tomorrow. Need to lock success criteria and call out any enterprise blockers (PHI, retention, on-prem).

alex: Key asks from customer: PHI-safe hosting (VPC/on-prem), KMS, latency p95 <= 200ms for UI flows, cost goal <= $0.15/1k tokens, acceptance = structured claim extraction with >=90% precision on their eval set.

sam: 200ms p95 depends heavily on token length. For <=512 tokens likely; for 2k-4k tokens we'll need different profile. We'll propose two model variants.

lee: Recommend two-track approach:
- low-latency track: quantized 8B for interactive UI (target p95 <= 200ms for <=1024 tokens)
- batch track: larger model on dedicated nodes for heavy claim processing (higher latency ok)
Also enable prefix/KV caching for repeated patient prefixes.

maria: They require endpoints in their VPC and KMS integration. Security flagged retention: customer wants max 30d. @irene can you confirm what we can offer for Private/VPC/on-prem?

irene: Default hosted retention is 90d, but Private/VPC can be configured down to 0 (no retention). On-prem obviously customer-controlled. I'll add these options to the sec answers doc and call out KMS/HSM support.

alex: Draft eval plan: customer will supply ~500 annotated prompts. We'll run our scoring harness. Proposed acceptance thresholds: F1 >= 0.88, latency p95 <= 200ms (interactive), cost per convo <= $0.12. Are these realistic?

sam: F1 0.88 on medical NER/extraction is aggressive for base open weights without fine-tune. Suggest fallback: if F1 between 0.82-0.88, allow a 2-week tuning window and re-evaluation. If <0.82, propose fine-tune budget or user acceptance thresholds.

lee: Cost note: POC on Dedicated with 2x A100 (or equivalent) estimated ~ $4k/week for continuous runs. If they insist <$2k/week we need smaller nodes or batching, which will push latency up. I'll run a precise cost calc.

maria: They also sent a security questionnaire (encryption, KMS, SOC2, ISO27001). We should attach the compliance packet and ask for any platform exceptions.

irene: I'll attach SOC2 summary, ISO attestation, and our data handling one-pager. For KMS we support AWS KMS + customer-managed HSM; will add key rotation runbook.

alex: Proposed timeline: Kickoff 2026-03-30, data ingest 1 week, eval runs 2 weeks, tuning 1 week = ~4 weeks total. Contingent on them delivering labeled prompts on day 1.

sam: If labeled prompts are late, shift by the same delay. Also decision point: model pinning. Recommend pin to model-2026-02-hc for reproducibility in acceptance tests.

maria: I'll assemble a POC acceptance checklist to send after the call. Quick ask: @lee can you post expected p95 numbers for the two models and the back-of-envelope cost breakdown?

lee: Numbers (back-of-envelope):
- gpt-neoX-8B-quant: p95 ~ 120ms for <=512 tokens, ~220ms for 1024 tokens; est $0.08/1k tokens.
- large-30B-dedicated: p95 ~ 340ms (interactive), est $0.45/1k tokens.
I'll DM the full cost table and a sensitivity chart (batch size vs latency).

alex: Example eval command we'll run internally: 
```
eval.run(
  model = "model-2026-02-hc",
  prompts = "healthco_eval.jsonl",
  metrics = ["precision","recall","f1","latency_p95"]
)
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled a dev test run for model-2026-02-hc on dev cluster at 2026-03-28T14:00Z.

maria: Great — thanks all. I'll share the checklist + security packet by EOD and confirm the kickoff agenda.

alex: +1. Also add an explicit acceptance clause: if interactive p95 exceeds 200ms for >=10% of eval queries, we escalate to fallback variant (quantized model) in the runbook.

sam: Noted. I'll prepare the fallback orchestration snippet for the runbook.

maria: Perfect — we should be ready for the call.
